lines.text: Welcome to Level 2! Today you will stop rewriting the same messages and build templates that do the work for you.
In Level 1 you saved good prompts.
A template goes one step further, because it has blanks called placeholders, like Customer name or Due date in square brackets.
You write it carefully once, and then you only fill the blanks each week.
A prompt template is what you paste into the AI, such as your monthly update prompt.
A message template is the finished text with merge fields, such as a fee reminder with a blank for the first name.
The AI helps you write both, but only you fill in the real details.
Mail merge joins one message template with a list in a sheet, so each person gets their own name, amount and date.
The AI writes the template, and your sheet fills in the names.
The AI never needs to see your real customer list.
Before sending, read at least three finished messages.
Look for empty blanks, wrong amounts and a field name the AI quietly changed.
Then send one test to yourself first.
Keep all your templates in one place, such as a Google Doc, a sheet, or saved templates in Gmail or Outlook.
For each one, note when to use it, its placeholders, and what to check.
A colleague should be able to pick it up and use it safely.
Here the front desk of a coaching centre asks for a fee reminder with four merge fields.
The prompt says to keep the field names exactly, and not to add any new facts.
The reminder is short and polite, but look closely at the last field.
The AI changed Due Date to just Date, so the merge would leave a gap.
We fix the field name before we save it, and that one check saves forty broken messages.
Now the sheet does the personal part, and the AI only writes the formula.
We describe the columns and give one example of the finished message.
The formula joins the pieces of text, and the TEXT part makes the amount and date look neat.
Drag it down, and every row gets its own message, while the real list never left the sheet.
Save your best message templates where you write emails, in Gmail or Outlook.
For mail merge, Word and Outlook work together, and some Google Workspace accounts have it inside Gmail.
If you have neither, the sheet formula already made every message for you.
Whatever tool you use, preview three messages and send a test to yourself first.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
